interpretation: 'When someone asked whether it is white says no, he has denied nothing other than its being [white]; and the denial is not-being.' Read semantically: the negative answer is exactly the negation of what was asked, so an answer to a yes/no question is the affirmation or the denial and leaves no third answer. Not formalized: the intuitionist agrees that negation is the only alternative answer; the dispute is over whether every question must already have one, which this sentence does not address.
